name: Broadleaf plantain
habitat: Compacted ground — footpaths, lawns, driveways, playing fields, the edge of any trail. It follows human traffic, which is why it is nearly always within reach of where you got hurt.
identify: Basal rosette of oval (P. major) or narrow lance-shaped (P. lanceolata) leaves, flat to the ground.
Three to seven PARALLEL veins running the length of the leaf — unusual for a broadleaf plant and the surest mark.
Pull a leaf slowly apart and the veins string out like tiny threads.
A leafless flower stalk carrying a dense narrow spike of tiny brownish flowers.

lookalikes.name: Common dock / sorrel seedlings
lookalikes.danger: Harmless, but it is not plantain and does not do the same job.
lookalikes.tell: Dock leaves have a single strong midrib with branching side veins, not parallel veins, and often a papery sheath at the leaf base.

lookalikes.name: Hosta and other ornamental rosettes
lookalikes.danger: Harmless to handle; some ornamentals are toxic if eaten.
lookalikes.tell: Garden setting, much larger fleshy leaves, and no flower spike of the plantain type.

preparations.method: Chew a clean leaf to a pulp and press it on the spot; cover with a whole leaf and hold.
preparations.for_use: Stings, bites, nettle rash, splinters and small infected-looking wounds — the classic drawing poultice.

preparations.method: Simmer a good handful of leaf in water for 10 minutes and cool.
preparations.for_use: Rinsing a graze or an irritated eye area.

preparations.method: Young leaves eaten raw; older leaves cooked (they get stringy).

cautions: Do not harvest from roadside verges, sprayed lawns, or ground fouled by animals — plantain grows precisely where traffic and spray are heaviest.
A poultice is comfort and mild antisepsis, not treatment for an established infection.
Rare allergic reactions; the pollen is a known allergen.
evidence: Very widespread traditional use for stings and minor wounds; laboratory support for anti-inflammatory and antibacterial constituents (aucubin, allantoin). Human trials are limited.
